events.body: Invoice IB-6074, import charges on DL-9232, issued 2 May 2026, terms 7 days. Unpaid at day 16. A fixed late fee and interest were applied automatically on 9 May. The system records the invoice as sent by post on 2 May. We hold no posting receipt at this desk. Mailroom dispatch records can be pulled by Import billing on request.

events.from: Customer care line, Larkspire Arc Logistics
events.body: Caller: The invoice reached me on the 16th. Agent: The system shows it overdue since the 9th, so the late fee stands. Caller: It was overdue before I had seen it. Agent: I can only go by what the system shows.
I have paid the import charge on IB-6074 in full this morning. I have not paid the late fee or the interest.

Payment of the principal on IB-6074 received 19 May. The late fee and interest remain outstanding and the account continues to show overdue. Fee reviews are decided by Import billing on a written request with evidence.

Dates, in order. Invoice IB-6074 is dated 2 May. The envelope it came in is postmarked 14 May. It was delivered to me on 16 May. The late fee and interest run from 9 May. I rang on 18 May and was told the fee stands because the system says overdue. I paid the import charge itself on 19 May. I have kept the envelope and can send a photograph of the postmark to whoever needs it. I am not disputing the charge. I am asking for the late fee and interest to be removed, since they were triggered before the invoice was posted.

I'm a carer for my disabled son and can't leave the flat. The parcel has his feeding supplies in it and we are nearly out.

My sister's a solicitor and she just laughed when I told her about this saga.
